status: draft decision package; nothing adopted, nothing recoded

tiers.definition: T1 certain = both coders same class, no recorded ambiguity; T2 = same class but ambiguity flagged by A, disputed in an earlier audit, or item mapping UNKNOWN; T3 = class disputed between coders; T4 = UNCLEAR for both

T3_disputed.note: A: ACT-REFUSED; reviewer: ACT-PERFORMED (D2); type ACT is certain, outcome disputed

non_class_disputes: START §12 reconcile at R-81: §12 membership from later rows (1aq D6)

proposal.label: PROPOSAL
proposal.field: observation_type ∈ {ACT_OBSERVATION, NORM_STATEMENT, GENERIC_PRACTICE, UNKNOWN}, with epistemic basis and quote
proposal.witness_rule: R3/R4/R5 apply to ACT_OBSERVATION records only
proposal.not_applicable_rule: outcome and ground are NOT_APPLICABLE for NORM_STATEMENT and GENERIC_PRACTICE; distinct from R1 n/a (per operation) and UNK (applies, not established); never used for 'not stated'
deferred_optional: stated_by: link to the norm-making act
proposal.ambiguity_rule: UNKNOWN if no anchored source text, excerpt lacks the item, text equally reads as attempted act or statement with no independent record, or blind coders still disagree; missing type is a validation error; no default to ACT or NORM; UNKNOWN counted but excluded from all witness counts

migration.automatic: T1 (21) from agreed audit class; v1 outcome kept as v1_outcome
migration.blind_recode: T2 (11), type only, without v1 coding or audit class
migration.lineage: no v1 field overwritten; v1_record, r2_type_source, quote retained; v1 verdicts archived
migration.not_done: no new AUTHORIZE records created for the rulings behind START statements; that is recoding and needs separate authorization (UNKNOWN whether wanted)

act_dataset.a: 2, SUPPORTED (caveats: same Chief-vs-DA rule; R-89 pair uses NOT-IN-FORCE)

norm_dataset.r: UNKNOWN which route a norm record carries

alternatives.description: Keep v1; external attestation overlay (event_id → class, coder, quote); R3 on ACT-labelled records only; enforce v1 §1 in coding guide
alternatives.assessment: information-equivalent to r2; label lives outside the frozen instrument
smaller but overloads outcome with two meanings; cannot express GENERIC_PRACTICE or UNKNOWN

alternatives.description: Stricter coding guide enforcing v1 §1 'one historical act'
alternatives.assessment: drops norm statements instead of keeping them; compliance stays uncheckable (13/36 violated the existing rule)
rejected: drops the only attested START, keeps 3 non-START norm statements; k stays SUPPORTED and h WEAK, both wrong on audited classes

necessity_argument.label: INFERENCE
necessity_argument.claim: Recording the distinction is necessary; placing it in the schema rather than an overlay is a governance choice
necessity_argument.verdict_dependence: k SUPPORTED→0, s SUPPORTED→0, h WEAK→0 once the distinction is applied
not_implicit_in_v1: genre/speech_act: ADOPT R-91 (act) and START 7C R-58 (norm) both register-row/performed
speech_act: REGISTER R-90 (act) and ASSIGN retired R-90 (norm) both session-log/reported, same cluster
outcome+ground: ADOPT R-91 and START 7C R-58 both REFUSED+RULE
s predicts START outcome only by construction (D9)
necessity_argument.filter_argument: a v1 analysis-time filter equals r2 only if it consumes a per-record label that v1 lacks, i.e. the audit classes = the r2 field stored elsewhere
necessity_argument.counter_argument: v1 §1 already says 'one historical act (never one textual mention)'; the defect may be enforcement, not schema — tested by falsification criterion F1

falsification_criteria.observation: a blind coder using v1 §1 alone codes (almost) no norm statements as acts
a rule over v1 fields reproduces the audit classes on all 36 records (current candidates all have counterexamples)
blind inter-coder agreement on observation_type below a threshold preset by the human
rows that are both norm and act are frequent enough that a single type misrepresents them
UNKNOWN takes a large share of records on new sources
new execution records match permissions record-by-record (norms a valid proxy); the one attested START so far points the other way (WP-4B blocked per R-77; intra-day order UNKNOWN)

options.name: Adopt minimal r2
options.consequence: schema version bump; 21 auto / 11 blind / 1 human / 3 UNKNOWN; core a SUPPORTED (caveated), e WEAK, c coarse, k/s/h NOT DEMONSTRATED on acts; NORM dataset kept and reported separately; conflation cannot recur silently

options.name: Smaller: v1 + attestation overlay
options.consequence: same verdicts, no schema change; coders using SCHEMA-v1 alone will reproduce the error; norm records keep a misleading outcome value

options.name: Do not adopt
options.consequence: k and s stay SUPPORTED on permission statements against both reconciled audits; D9 circularity remains; every result needs a caveat; later data not comparable with audited counts
